titleCard.title: Sift
titleCard.subtitle: Twelve bids for the same job. The low one is $52,500 under the winner. Is it a better deal, or is it pricing less work?

closeCard.title: The agent recommends. The human decides.
closeCard.subtitle: A real Strands Swarm, AgentSkills, Context Injection and GoalLoop, on top of a deterministic core the model never touches.

beats.title: The answer you can sign
lines: Ask a chatbot which of twelve contractor bids to take and you'll have an answer in ten seconds. Confident. Plausible. And if you're the one signing the award, you can't use it.
Sift is built for the answer you can sign. You say what matters. It works out what has to be established before it answers, establishes it, and tells you what it couldn't.

beats.title: Two Strands topologies
lines: Under the hood it's the Strands SDK, twice over. Where the order of work is a routing problem, a Swarm. That's bids, and home energy.

beats.title: Two Strands topologies
lines: Where the order is fixed, a Graph. That's the car purchase. Three decision packs, one engine, and a pack is just data.

beats.title: The core the model never touches
lines: The scoring is a separate deterministic core. One dependency. No model, no network, no filesystem.
So every number you're about to check was never touched by a model. Everything above that line is Strands.

beats.title: Twelve bids for the same job
lines: Twelve plumbing bids for a school renovation. Cedar and Sons is cheapest, by fifty-two and a half thousand. It also prices sixty-two and a half percent of the required scope.
Better deal, or pricing less work?

beats.title: A Swarm, steered mid-run
lines: One click starts a real Strands Swarm. Six specialists, five handoffs, each one a real handoff event from the SDK.
Each specialist loads only the skill its job needs. Four activations.
And every turn, a context injector hands it the weights, the open gaps and the budget. Twenty-eight injections.

beats.title: A Swarm, steered mid-run
lines: Watch the scope analyst. Completed, redirected once.
It was circling the same two bids, so a Guide intervention pointed it at the third.

beats.title: Refused before it ran
lines: Here's a Deny. The price analyst reached for the licence lookup, a tool this pack grants only to the credential checker. Refused before it ran.
Not a failure. A boundary, recorded as one.

beats.title: The agent refuses to answer
lines: Now the part that matters. GoalLoop runs the recommendation through a validator, and the validator throws out the first draft.
It ranked twelve bids that weren't on a common basis yet. Not a bad answer. A false one.
So it goes round again. Most tools would have shipped that ranking. This one refuses.

beats.title: The cheapest bid isn't
lines: Here's the maths, and you can check it. Cedar is silent on three things the others price. Permits, eighteen thousand. Shower-valve rough-in, thirty-one five. Haul-away, six thousand.
Corrected, Cedar is two seventy-nine against Northgate's two seventy-six. The bid that looked fifty-two thousand cheaper is three thousand more.

beats.title: Unknown stays unknown
lines: It names a winner and still won't close two questions: a scope comparison that came back incomplete, and two bids that failed credential checks.
Unknown doesn't get rounded up to fine.

beats.title: Scores highest. Still doesn't win.
lines: Change what you care about and the ranking moves. That's the deterministic core, not the model.
And the sixth criterion has no slider. Credentials are set by the pack. You can't weight your way past them.

beats.title: Scores highest. Still doesn't win.
lines: Now Two Rivers scores highest of all twelve. Ninety-one percent, against the winner's seventy-two. And it still doesn't win.
Flagged, not removed. Still ranked, and still yours to decide.

beats.title: The person decides, on camera
lines: Awarding is gated by a Confirm intervention. The proposal sits pending, with no approving actor, until a person acts.
So I act. Select Northgate Plumbing.
Decided. The agent recommended. A human awarded. That line is structural.

beats.title: Proof it is really Strands
lines: This is the Runtime Inspector. Every tool call, model call, node and handoff comes through the SDK's own lifecycle hooks, under one trace id.
Four hundred and thirty-three events. A hundred and five spans, every one stamped with the SDK's own instrumentation scope.
And every mechanism you just watched has a test that fails if it stops being true.

beats.title: Live, on Amazon Bedrock
lines: And here's how a bid actually gets in. Drop the PDF, and a real model reads it.
That's Amazon Nova, on Amazon Bedrock. Six values read off the document, and it says plainly it couldn't read two.
Quoted total, two hundred and forty-one thousand eight hundred. Read by a model. Confidence forty percent. Not verified. Only a person can verify.
It refused to rank twelve bids until they were comparable. Flagged the highest scorer instead of hiding it. Left the award to a person.
That's an answer you can sign.
